Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

person.segment_label: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

observation.payment_scope: One existing member's basic fare only; all other payments are outside this decision.
observation.inventory_rule: Simultaneous intentions, no seat reserved; allocation is cleared in a recorded order afterwards.

analysis.summary: All 16 members declined; none bought. Fifteen cite no ticket both available and within their basic-fare budget (environment-forced), and one (DEAL-1126-00011) declines from low trip interest and preference for keeping schedule and money, not a price objection. No customer states the fare itself is unaffordable. With zero purchases and no genuine price objection, the feedback does not support a directional fare change; inventory and interest, not fare level, dominate.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 632 HKD fare on fresh members will yield conversion no different from the current round; if a lower fare materially raises conversion, this hypothesis is contradicted.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 223 HKD member fare, 13 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below their stated ceilings. Three declined mainly for low trip interest or low destination appeal after recent travel, not because the fare was unaffordable. No inventory denials occurred and capacity was not binding. The evidence shows strong conversion at a low fare but does not establish that a higher fare would retain enough buyers, since buyers repeatedly said they would refuse the 790 normal fare.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce conversion enough that basic ticket receipts do not increase versus the current low fare, because buyers repeatedly anchor their purchase to the bargain price rather than destination appeal.

analysis.summary: At the 223 HKD member fare, 12 of 16 customers bought, citing a compelling bargain well below their budgets and the 790 HKD regular fare. Three declined mainly for low trip interest or recent travel, not price; one was blocked by budget/inventory constraints. No customer objected to the fare itself. The current price sits well below the 632 HKD cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus the current 223 HKD fare, since buyers cited large budget headroom and rejected the 790 HKD regular fare.

analysis.summary: Six of sixteen members bought at the 387 HKD fare, citing a compelling discount versus the 790 HKD regular fare; all said they would decline at the regular fare. Five declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available ticket, and five were optional-trip or low-destination-appeal declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 387 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above those at 387 HKD, since buyers cited the discount as decisive and no customer objected to price.

analysis.summary: At the current member fare of 323 HKD, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. All declines cite low trip interest, weak destination appeal, or a preference for keeping money and free time, not the fare itself; three declines are inventory/budget-forced. Buyers repeatedly describe 323 as a bargain and say they would refuse the 790 normal fare. No customer objects to the fare level, so the evidence does not support lowering price. The paired initial at 632 HKD converted far worse, but that is aggregate context, not fresh evidence.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts enough to offset the higher per-ticket revenue, because current buyers treat 323 HKD as well below their stated ceilings and declines are driven by low interest rather than fare.

analysis.summary: At the current 324 HKD member fare, five members bought and ten declined. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and four were low-interest or optional-trip objections rather than price objections. Buyers explicitly cited the fare as compelling versus the 790 normal fare. No decline was primarily a price objection, so the evidence does not support lowering the fare; buyers' enthusiasm at 324 suggests testing a higher fare is plausible, though buying now does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because current buyers cite the fare as a strong bargain well below their budgets.

analysis.summary: At the 305 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), not price objections. Three declines cited low trip interest or destination appeal despite finding the fare affordable. All buyers stressed the fare was far below the 790 HKD normal fare and would not pay that. analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases that basic ticket receipts rise versus 305 HKD, since no cited decline was a price objection and buyers cited large discounts below the 790 HKD normal fare.

analysis.summary: At the current 290 HKD member fare, 12 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below their stated ceilings and the 790 HKD normal fare. Two declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest optional browsers who found the fare affordable but the trip unappealing. No customer objected to the price itself. The fare sits well below the 632 HKD cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus 290 HKD, since current buyers cite large gaps between the fare and their stated ceilings.

analysis.summary: At HKD 289, 10 of 16 members bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain below their stated ceilings and below the HKD 790 regular fare. Three declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available ticket, and three were low-interest optional-trip declines where price was affordable but appeal was weak. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 289 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the HKD 2,890 baseline, since current buyers cite large headroom below their stated ceilings.

validation.adoption_rule: Candidate needs positive paired mean and descriptive lower bounds against initial and no-offer, with no negative held-out world; otherwise retain initial or report no offer. Not human-market statistical certification.
validation.scope: One purchase opportunity per member at the chosen flight snapshot, not annual membership profit.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
